title: The Ledger
logline: A village shop's handwritten credit book holds decades of small debts, some paid next week, some after the harvest, some quietly struck through when the debtor dies.
human_question: Does everything we owe, or are owed, eventually come due?

situation.what_happens: A small shop extends credit to the households around it and records it by hand. Over a season the book fills and empties unevenly: some accounts are cleared every week, some wait for a harvest or a pay day, some are carried for years out of relationship rather than expectation, and some are quietly ended, because a family has moved away or because the person has died and nobody will be asked. The shopkeeper does not think of this as philosophy. It is how the shop stays open.
situation.who_is_involved: The shopkeeper, who is lender, record keeper and the person who decides when to stop asking; the households who buy on credit, who are neighbours as well as debtors; and whoever in the family will inherit both the shop and the book.
situation.what_is_at_stake: The shop's survival, and the standing of families whose names are in the book. For the shopkeeper, the working question of how long to carry someone. For the customers, dignity: a credit book is a private record of a household's worst months, kept by someone they see every day.
situation.how_it_unfolds: Credit builds through a season and settles after it, unevenly, and the pressure arrives when the shop's own suppliers want paying. A line gets struck through when it is clear nothing more will come, and that moment is almost never announced. Reality decides which accounts close, which simply lapse, and whether the shop has a good year at all.

concept_merge.why_together: One concept carries this film and needs no partner to be felt. Time of ripening (C057) sorts what a person does by when its result arrives: now, next, much later whenever an occasion opens, or never. A shop's credit book is that same sorting done by an ordinary person with a pen. The film's work is to let the two sit beside each other without either becoming an illustration of the other.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That what comes due runs on several clocks and is not a balance. Some things arrive at once, some sit for years waiting for an opening that may never come, and some simply expire, which the source is careful to call expiry rather than forgiveness. Watching this happen with money makes the shape visible without asking anyone to believe anything.

concept_links.why: The source's own image for action that never ripens is seed grain kept past its season, which will not sprout [C057-P:L87], and the digest insists that lapsing is expiry, not forgiveness or a clean slate. A credit book in which some debts are paid, some wait for an occasion and some are struck through gives that its plainest secular form. The digest also rules out 'instant karma' and any reading in which good and bad net out, so the accounting image must never become a moral balance sheet, and no customer's poverty is framed as anything but circumstance.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: The texts teach that what we do does not all come due at the same time: some of it shows up in this life, some in the next, some waits a very long time for an opening, and some simply lapses and never comes due at all.
what_must_be_real: The shop's actual trade, and its customers' privacy: no name, amount or household appears identifiably without that person's own consent, and nobody is filmed being refused credit. The shopkeeper decides what the book may show, and can withdraw a page at any point.
position_hint: middle: the group's plainest and least ceremonial account of how results keep different clocks, placed where the films turn from rites to mechanisms.
risks: Exposing named debtors or a family's money troubles to their own neighbours
Letting the ledger image suggest that good and bad net out, which the sources deny
Poverty or a run of bad years read as the result of someone's past actions
The metaphor overwhelming the shopkeeper's actual livelihood
drop_if: Customers' privacy cannot be protected while the book is still legible as a story
No shop with a long-running handwritten credit system will take part
The shopkeeper would have to perform the book for the camera

connections.note: A gate and a ledger are two everyday images for the same family of ideas about what comes due; the cattle-pen idea has been merged into IDEA-0136, where the ordering question belongs to a real deathbed.
Both ask what happens to what is still owed or unfinished when the person concerned is gone.

selection.reason: Used by its episode and directly supported by the C057 digest's own central image.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
